data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describing it when the test's installation ritual embeds the subject's failure as a precondition for registration \u2014 the 3-of-26 result arises because only mutations that participate in the shown-to-fail-first installation path are visible to the guard, while the 1/9 compile.py loss and the 4/4 to 6/7 module spread reflect the same mechanism applied at different registry scopes.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 3 surviving mutations would still be caught under a naive no-install test run, the installation ritual is not the differentiator.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 compile.py loss is attributable to a one-line content-edit hole with no registry involvement, then the distribution is noise, not a fingerprint.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If independent re-runs with shuffled mutation order change which 3 of 26 survive, the result is order-dependent rather than structurally constrained.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If every ordinarily-guarded module's 4/4 to 6/7 spread is explained by module size alone, then the constraint is coverage, not ritual.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The shown-to-fail-first installation pattern means the test suite is not measuring the code as written but as installed through a ritual that already encodes which failures count. When a mutation is introduced, the guard sees only the delta against the canonical failure registry, not the full behavioral surface. The distribution (3 of 26) is the fingerprint of a registry whose entries are selected by the same author's care in the same week: mutations that land outside the ritual's blast radius are invisible by construction.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
